gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-parkinsans: Loud, spaced-out and a bit cheeky, Early GameBoy stretches its tracking wide with only a modest thick-thin shift. Parkinsans keeps one stroke thickness throughout, its lowercase rising close to the capitals, so paragraphs stay crisp when shrunk.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-preahvihear: Preahvihear gapes open like a pried oyster shell, with a lofty x-height that gives its lowercase real presence on the line. Early GameBoy brings the commanding, playful spacing up top.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-pt-sans-capt: PT Sans Caption lets its bowls stay unclosed and inviting, with big-bodied lowercase that fills the line generously. Early GameBoy handles the shouting; the text face handles the reading.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-radio-canada: Playful up top, Early GameBoy loosens its tracking and lets curves swell gently. Radio Canada Big follows below with a monoline skeleton and an x-height that fills the line, a sturdy counterweight to the heading's gentle swelling.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-sintony: Brash and playful, Early GameBoy spaces itself out with a modest thick-thin shift and a high x-height line. Sintony follows with a chunky, tall midzone and curves that never clog.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-stack-sans-n: Early GameBoy leads with spread-out tracking and curves that thicken and thin gently, commanding yet playful. Stack Sans Notch settles in underneath, drawing rod-stock horizontals and verticals of identical thickness, with curves you can see into.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-abeezee: Classic from the first letter, Edo SZ has lowercase with cast iron stature. It does its best work big and short, while ABeeZee follows with neon-tube thickness and terminals that stop well away from the stem.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-amiko: Amiko reads modern and plain-spoken, its terminals flaring outward like tongs. Edo SZ is at its best with round bowls whose walls never swell, while Amiko is at its best in crayon-thick lowercase.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-anek-bangla: Classic in posture, Edo SZ holds one constant stroke width with no calligraphic swell on any downstroke. Anek Bangla sits alongside with wide s curves barely curled in and a short stretch from midline to ascender.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-anek-odia: Cast-iron classic, Edo SZ looks drawn by a fixed-width nib. Anek Odia joins it with rounds left unsealed like an unlatched hook, and capitals only slightly above lowercase.
